messages:
alex: heads up — after the kernel-selection tweak merged in PR #8123, we're seeing a host-side CPU burn for small streaming requests. latency p50 unchanged but p99 up ~30ms and host CPU up ~18%. digging in.

maria: oh no, which heuristic change? the fanout-to-simd threshold? :eyes:

alex: yep. changed boundary so the runtime picks vectorized matmul even for seq_len < 32 in some cases. suspicion: increased memcpy / conversion overhead for tiny KV hits and more frequent chunk emission.

sam: can you paste the flamegraph or perf top snippet? also are we seeing more syscalls/writev churn?

alex: attaching perf flame excerpt:
```
# perf script snippet
runtime_worker  [.] emit_chunk
runtime_worker  [.] tokenize_fragment
runtime_worker  [.] memcpy
runtime_worker  [.] grpc::Write
runtime_worker  [.] SerializeProto
``` 
seems emit_chunk -> SerializeProto -> grpc write path dominates.

riley: that lines up with traces we saw in canary. If SerializeProto grows, small-frame traffic causes more gRPC packets. maybe missing writev coalescing after proto change.

alex: also noticed kvcache hit-rate steady but KV decode time per hit up 2.2x. sample from strace showed many small writes (64-256B) to socket.

infra-qa: deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-15T10:08 completed on ring-2.

maria: quick experiment idea: 1) revert kernel boundary locally, 2) increase emission watermark (emit when buffer >= 1kB or EOS), 3) enable writev coalesce in host proxy. Which is easiest? 

sam: (3) is low-risk, I can toggle coalesce flag in proxy and test on canary. also try bumping grpc max_send_message_length? might change packetization.

alex: I'm going to run microbench: batch sizes [1..16], seq_len [8,16,24], record host CPU, syscall counts, and grpc packet sizes. will paste results.

alex: raw microbench results (summary):
```
seq=8 batch=1 cpu=62% syscalls=420 pkt_avg=180B p99_lat=210ms
seq=8 batch=4 cpu=48% syscalls=160 pkt_avg=520B p99_lat=160ms
seq=24 batch=1 cpu=33% syscalls=90  pkt_avg=1100B p99_lat=120ms
``` 
small seq & single batch is worst.

riley: thinking: kernel-selection should factor downstream emission cost: a kernel that speeds compute but increases output fragmentation is net negative. maybe add utility function: net_cost = compute_ms + alpha * emitted_packets.

maria: +1. also add KV decode cost into selection signal. we have metric kvcache_decode_ms per-hit.

sam: I opened a tiny PR to add writev coalesce + bump emission watermark to 1KB by default on hostproxy: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/987. canary looks promising.

alex: great. can you also add a telemetry event when protocol emits <256B frames so we can alert if regression recurs?

sam: yes will add a counter and per-route drop-in chart.

alex: thanks. next steps: (a) run canary with coalesce + watermark, (b) instrument selection logic to include emitted_packet_estimate, (c) add alert for mini-frame spike. I'll follow up with numbers.

maria: thanks team. :thumbsup:
